targets.authors: Szabó-Bódi, B.; Kasza, G.; Szakos, D.
targets.title: Assessment of household food waste in Hungary
targets.evidence_quote: The actual study is a replication of the first Hungarian measurement-based research conducted in 2016 [24], which we regarded as a baseline for comparison.
targets.outcome_quote: The constitution of food waste in the households was found to be very similar, indicating a dominant rate of avoidable food waste (an actual share of 48.82% compared to 48.70% in 2016), followed by the unavoidable part (47.05% compared to 47.13% in 2016). Potentially avoidable food waste remained under 5% in both periods.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly compare the repeated national measurement with the baseline and report very similar composition and the same ranking of discarded foods. The small temporal decrease is interpreted as campaign progress, not failure of the earlier finding. FUSIONS is a methodology source, not another target.
